projects.title: Build a solar powered rover
projects.description: Design a solar-powered rover that can explore rough terrain and collect environmental data.

brief.challenge: How might a small rover travel across uneven ground while collecting useful environmental readings?
brief.concept: Build a low-voltage rover with a solar-assisted power system, motor control and a simple sensor payload. Compare what the solar panel can actually supply with the motors’ demand, then test the rover outdoors.
brief.outcome: A moving prototype, a wiring and power budget, and a short field-test report.
materials: Small solar panel and charge controller
Motor driver, geared motors and chassis

phases.title: Define the mission
phases.detail: Choose a surface, a useful sensor reading and a realistic operating time.

phases.title: Design the system
phases.detail: Sketch the power path, estimate motor demand and choose a safe low-voltage architecture.

phases.title: Build and program
phases.detail: Assemble the chassis, control movement and record sensor readings.

phases.title: Test and improve
phases.detail: Compare runtime, mobility and sensor readings under different light conditions.

criteria: Moves through the chosen test course
brief.stretch: Add an obstacle warning and compare energy use before and after your changes.
brief.note: Keep the build low voltage. Use an appropriate battery charger and teacher supervision for wiring and testing.

projects.title: Smart irrigation system
projects.description: Design a low-cost irrigation system that conserves water and keeps crops healthy.

brief.challenge: How can a school garden use less water without leaving plants dry?
brief.concept: Measure soil conditions, decide when watering is needed and build a small demonstration that controls or signals irrigation. Start with a container garden so results are easy to observe.
brief.outcome: A garden prototype and a record comparing soil readings and water use.

phases.title: Observe the garden
phases.detail: Identify the plants, watering pattern and when the soil is too dry.

phases.title: Set a threshold
phases.detail: Compare sensor readings in dry and watered soil and choose a trigger point.

phases.title: Make the prototype
phases.detail: Connect the sensor to an indicator or small low-voltage pump.

phases.title: Measure the difference
phases.detail: Track watering events and adjust the threshold to avoid overwatering.

criteria: Responds to a change in soil moisture
brief.stretch: Add a simple rainfall observation so watering can be delayed after rain.
brief.note: Keep electronics away from water and use a supervised low-voltage supply.

projects.title: Portable solar charger
projects.description: Build a rugged portable charger for small devices using solar energy.

brief.challenge: What would it take to charge a small device when wall power is unavailable?
brief.concept: Design a protected, portable solar charging prototype. Work out the load first, then compare panel output and stored energy against the charging goal.
brief.outcome: A low-voltage charger prototype and measured charging performance.
materials: Compatible charge controller and protected storage

phases.title: Define the load
phases.detail: Choose a small target device and calculate its approximate energy need.

phases.title: Plan the power chain
phases.detail: Map the panel, controller, storage and regulated output.

phases.title: Assemble and measure
phases.detail: Build the low-voltage system and record output in different sunlight.

phases.title: Evaluate
phases.detail: Compare charging time with your estimate and explain any losses.

brief.stretch: Compare two panel orientations and graph their output.
brief.note: Use a compatible protected battery and charge controller. Never connect a device directly to an unregulated panel.

projects.title: Air quality monitor
projects.description: Measure and map air quality around your school or community.

brief.challenge: How can we identify places and times when local air conditions change?
brief.concept: Collect readings with a sensor prototype, label the conditions and explore patterns in a simple map or chart. Treat low-cost sensor readings as indicative, not regulatory measurements.
brief.outcome: A sensor logger and a short, clearly qualified data story.

phases.title: Choose a question
phases.detail: Pick locations or times to compare and define what a reading can mean.

phases.title: Capture readings
phases.detail: Log readings with time, place and contextual observations.

phases.title: Analyze
phases.detail: Clean and chart the readings, noting sensor limitations and outliers.

phases.title: Communicate
phases.detail: Explain the pattern without overstating health or regulatory conclusions.

brief.stretch: Compare indoor and outdoor trends over several days.
brief.note: This is an educational monitor, not a medical or certified air-quality instrument.

projects.title: Build a school attendance app
projects.description: Create a web app to track attendance and generate useful reports.

brief.challenge: How can a class record attendance accurately and see useful patterns without exposing student information?
brief.concept: Create a small web application for marking attendance, reviewing records and summarizing class participation. Design roles and privacy rules before building the interface.
brief.outcome: A usable app prototype, a data model and a short demonstration.

phases.title: Map the workflow
phases.detail: Interview a teacher about taking, correcting and viewing attendance.

phases.title: Design the data
phases.detail: Plan classes, learners, dates and attendance records with access rules.

phases.title: Build the core
phases.detail: Implement marking, editing and a simple summary view.

phases.title: Test with scenarios
phases.detail: Try absent, late and correction cases using fictional learners.

criteria: Saves records by date and class
brief.stretch: Add a weekly summary chart or export for a teacher.
brief.note: Use fictional learner data during development and get school approval before using real records.

projects.title: Design a solar charging station
projects.description: Build a solar-powered charging station for your school or community.

brief.challenge: Could a shared charging point serve a school reliably using solar energy?
brief.concept: Model a small solar charging station, estimate daily demand and prototype a protected low-voltage output. Show how usage and energy supply change through the day.
brief.outcome: A scale prototype, energy budget and usage plan.

phases.title: Estimate demand
phases.detail: Count expected devices and sketch a daily charging schedule.

phases.title: Size the prototype
phases.detail: Choose low-voltage components and map protection and connections.

phases.title: Build
phases.detail: Assemble the scale station and measure its regulated output.

phases.title: Review capacity
phases.detail: Compare measured supply with planned demand and identify limits.

brief.stretch: Design a fair booking or usage schedule for a class.
brief.note: This is a low-voltage learning prototype. Have qualified supervision before any building-scale installation.

projects.title: Create a flood warning system
projects.description: Use sensors to monitor water levels and send early alerts.

brief.challenge: How could a community notice rising water early enough to respond?
brief.concept: Build a tabletop water-level monitor that detects threshold crossings and alerts a nearby observer. Explore false alarms and the limits of a single sensor.
brief.outcome: A working tabletop alert and documented threshold tests.

phases.title: Define alert levels
phases.detail: Choose normal, warning and critical levels for a model channel.

phases.title: Wire and program
phases.detail: Read the sensor and activate visible and audible alerts.

phases.title: Test conditions
phases.detail: Repeat rising and falling water tests and record false triggers.

phases.title: Improve the warning
phases.detail: Adjust thresholds and explain backup and maintenance needs.

criteria: Detects set levels consistently in the model
brief.stretch: Add a local display or data log for recent water levels.
brief.note: A classroom prototype must not be relied on for real flood safety decisions.

projects.title: Make a line-following robot
projects.description: Build and program a robot to follow a line using sensors.

brief.challenge: How can a robot follow a route using only the contrast beneath it?
brief.concept: Make a small robot sense a dark line on a light surface, steer with two motors and improve its performance through repeatable trials.
brief.outcome: A line-following robot and measured route results.

phases.title: Create a course
phases.detail: Lay out a track with curves and a clear start and finish.

phases.title: Read the line
phases.detail: Calibrate sensor readings on light and dark surfaces.

phases.title: Make it move
phases.detail: Control the motors to correct left and right drift.

phases.title: Improve accuracy
phases.detail: Time multiple runs and adjust speed or sensor placement.

brief.stretch: Add a junction choice and explain how the robot decides its route.

projects.title: Train a crop disease detector
projects.description: Use computer vision to identify plant diseases from leaf images.

brief.challenge: Can a model identify visible leaf patterns while remaining honest about uncertainty?
brief.concept: Train an image classifier using an appropriately sourced dataset, compare results across classes and show what happens on unfamiliar images.
brief.outcome: A reproducible model experiment and an error analysis.

phases.title: Audit the data
phases.detail: Identify classes, sources, image quality and possible duplicates.

phases.title: Create a baseline
phases.detail: Split data by source and train a simple initial model.

phases.title: Evaluate honestly
phases.detail: Review per-class errors and examples the model gets wrong.

phases.title: Present limits
phases.detail: Explain where real field images differ from training images.

criteria: Explains at least two failure cases
brief.stretch: Compare performance with different lighting or backgrounds.
brief.note: Predictions are educational and should not replace agricultural advice or field diagnosis.

projects.title: Model a safe footbridge
projects.description: Design and analyze a bridge using CAD and simulation.

brief.challenge: How can a small crossing be modeled to carry a specified load safely?
brief.concept: Create a conceptual footbridge in CAD, define loads and compare design options with simplified analysis. Record assumptions and where professional review is needed.
brief.outcome: A CAD model, simplified calculations and a design review.

phases.title: Define the crossing
phases.detail: State the span, intended users and assumed loading conditions.

phases.title: Compare concepts
phases.detail: Sketch alternative structures and explain their load paths.

phases.title: Model and analyze
phases.detail: Create a CAD model and run simplified checks with stated assumptions.

phases.title: Review the design
phases.detail: Identify failure modes, accessibility and unanswered site questions.

brief.stretch: Compare material quantities between two structural options.
brief.note: This is a learning design, not construction approval. Real bridges require qualified engineering design and local approvals.

projects.title: Build a health monitoring device
projects.description: Prototype a device that measures heart rate and temperature.

brief.challenge: How can a prototype display pulse and temperature readings clearly without making medical claims?
brief.concept: Connect educational sensors to a low-voltage controller, display readings and compare repeatability under controlled conditions.
brief.outcome: A display prototype and a report on measurement limits.

phases.title: Define the display
phases.detail: Choose readable labels, units and a safe sensor placement.

phases.title: Read sensors
phases.detail: Capture readings and inspect noise or missing values.

phases.title: Build the interface
phases.detail: Display readings with clear status when data is unavailable.

phases.title: Check repeatability
phases.detail: Repeat measurements and discuss variation and limitations.

criteria: States that the readings are unvalidated
brief.stretch: Plot recent readings without storing personal identifiers.
brief.note: Educational prototype only. Do not use it to diagnose, monitor or make treatment decisions.

projects.title: Create a secure chat app
projects.description: Build an end-to-end encrypted chat app and learn security basics.

brief.challenge: How can two users exchange messages privately while understanding what encryption does and does not protect?
brief.concept: Build a prototype messaging flow using a well-established encryption library, then document identity, key handling and the remaining privacy risks. Never invent your own cryptographic algorithm.
brief.outcome: A demonstrable chat prototype and a threat model.

phases.title: Model the threats
phases.detail: Decide who should read messages and what the server may learn.

phases.title: Design identities
phases.detail: Plan account verification, keys and recovery before implementation.

phases.title: Build a prototype
phases.detail: Use a proven library for client-side encryption and message exchange.

phases.title: Review limitations
phases.detail: Test errors and document metadata, device and key-loss risks.

brief.stretch: Design a safe way for users to verify one another’s identity.
brief.note: This is an educational prototype. Do not promise production-grade end-to-end security without independent review.

courses.title: Electronics from zero
courses.description: Understand circuits, read simple schematics and build a working prototype.

lessons.title: Current, voltage and resistance
lessons.summary: Learn what each quantity measures and use Ohm’s law to estimate current before connecting a component.

lessons.title: Build a safe LED circuit
lessons.summary: Choose a resistor, connect an LED on a breadboard and test the polarity with a low-voltage supply.

lessons.title: Read a simple schematic
lessons.summary: Trace a circuit from its power source through each component, then draw your own build plan.

courses.title: Solar energy essentials
courses.description: Learn how solar systems work and design a safe small-scale setup.

lessons.title: From sunlight to electricity
lessons.summary: Explore how solar cells produce DC power and why orientation and shade affect output.

lessons.title: Estimate the energy you need
lessons.summary: Work out load power and daily energy before choosing a panel and battery.

lessons.title: Plan a small solar build
lessons.summary: Sketch the panel, charge controller, storage and load with suitable low-voltage protection.

courses.title: Arduino for makers
courses.description: Program and build interactive projects with sensors and actuators.

lessons.title: Your first sketch
lessons.summary: Understand setup, loop, digital inputs and outputs before uploading a program.

lessons.title: Read a sensor
lessons.summary: Connect a low-voltage sensor and inspect its readings using the serial monitor.

lessons.title: Control motion
lessons.summary: Use a motor driver and separate motor power supply to control speed and direction.

courses.title: Design with CAD
courses.description: Turn your ideas into precise models and test dimensions before building.

lessons.title: Sketch with dimensions
lessons.summary: Create a constrained sketch that captures the important measurements of a component.

lessons.title: Build a 3D model
lessons.summary: Use basic features to turn a sketch into a printable or manufacturable part.

lessons.title: Review and export
lessons.summary: Check fit and tolerances, then export the right file for sharing or fabrication.
